claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a homogeneous single-solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and yield strength.
Ti solute atoms introduce lattice distortions in CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti-induced lattice distortions promote enhanced or earlier dynamic recovery during deformation.
The atomic-size misfit associated with Ti lowers the barrier for dislocation cross-slip.
The atomic-size misfit associated with Ti promotes dislocation annihilation.
Enhanced dynamic recovery reduces the accumulation of dislocations during deformation.
Reduced dislocation accumulation limits strain hardening.
Limited strain hardening accounts for the lower hardness and yield strength of CoCrFeNiTi relative to CoCrFeNi.
The proposed controlled comparison is between equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and equimolar Ti-free CoCrFeNi under identical tensile or compression testing.
Using the same annealing or quenching treatment and strain rate ensures that observed differences arise solely from Ti-induced lattice distortion.
Under identical test conditions, CoCrFeNiTi will have lower yield strength than equimolar CoCrFeNi.
Under identical test conditions, CoCrFeNiTi will have lower hardness than equimolar CoCrFeNi.
After comparable deformation, CoCrFeNiTi will have a lower dislocation density than CoCrFeNi.
CoCrFeNiTi will show more microstructural evidence of dynamic recovery, cross-slip, or dislocation annihilation than CoCrFeNi.
The Ti-free CoCrFeNi baseline is expected to have higher work hardening than CoCrFeNiTi.
The hypothesis is restricted to single-phase solid solutions deformed at room temperature under quasi-static or moderate strain rates with grain-boundary effects minimized.
The quantitative contribution of dynamic recovery to the target alloy's mechanical properties is not established.
The hypothesis is falsified if CoCrFeNiTi lacks lower strength and hardness or lacks evidence of enhanced dynamic recovery relative to CoCrFeNi.

contradictions.description: The claim that differences would arise solely from Ti-induced lattice distortion is not secured by comparing equimolar CoCrFeNi with equimolar CoCrFeNiTi: adding Ti changes every non-Ti atomic fraction from 25 at.% to 20 at.% and may also change crystal structure or phase stability. Identical processing alone does not isolate lattice distortion from these compositional and structural effects.
